To extract the requested values from the provided surface tension vs. concentration chart:

1.  **Lowest concentration point:**
    The lowest concentration shown on the graph is the leftmost data point. By observing the logarithmic x-axis, this point is located at approximately $0.015\text{ mM}$ (midway between $10^{-2}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$). Looking at the linear y-axis, the grid lines are spaced by $10\text{ mN/m}$. The point lies slightly above the $60\text{ mN/m}$ line, roughly a quarter of the way to where the $70\text{ mN/m}$ line would be. This gives a surface tension of approximately $62.5\text{ mN/m}$.

2.  **Plateau region:**
    At the highest concentrations (from roughly $4\text{ mM}$ to $10\text{ mM}$), the curve flattens out into a plateau. The y-values for the last three points are roughly $27.5$, $27.8$, and $28.0\text{ mN/m}$. The average or representative surface tension in this region can be reasonably estimated as $\sim 28\text{ mN/m}$.

3.  **Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC):**
    The CMC is traditionally estimated as the intersection of the linearly declining pre-plateau region and the flat plateau region. 
    *   The pre-plateau points strongly follow a line: passing through $(0.6\text{ mM}, 36\text{ mN/m})$ and $(1.5\text{ mM}, 29.5\text{ mN/m})$.
    *   The plateau stabilizes around $27.5$ to $28\text{ mN/m}$.
    *   Extrapolating the linearly declining section down to a plateau level of roughly $27.5$ to $28\text{ mN/m}$ intersects the x-axis almost exactly at the first minor gridline after $10^{0}$, which represents $2.0\text{ mM}$.
